tag: Sprint 14 Task E, F117 (F114 cloud read)

bensberg-quantum-core-concept: Abstract, pp.1-2: the paper introduces and defines the quantum core concept; the value matches the passage.
bensberg-energy-decomposition-eq1: Section 2.3, Eq. (1), p.6: the paper writes the total energy as this sum of four terms.
bensberg-qm-energy-partition-eq2: Section 2.3, Eq. (2), p.6: the paper writes E_QM as quantum-core, environment and interaction terms.
bensberg-no-embedded-scf: Section 2.3, p.8: the paper states it skips the embedded SCF and uses the initial Kohn-Sham orbitals, with its two stated reasons.
bensberg-interaction-term-ks-densities: Section 2.3, p.8: the paper states that in practice only the KS orbital densities enter the interaction term, with its reason.
bensberg-mulliken-assignment-shift: Section 3.1, pp.10-11: 0.4 Mulliken threshold, assignment to the core of largest population, shift 1.0 au; all stated.
bensberg-electronic-structure-methods: Section 3.1, pp.10-11: PBE-D3(BJ)/def2-TZVP, DLPNO-CCSD(T0) NormalPNO, Serenity; all stated.
bensberg-quantum-cores-chosen: Sections 2.2 and 3.1: two manually chosen cores in the ligand, and the 150 kJ/mol window around the median QM/MM energy; stated as the paper's own choices.
bensberg-single-system-scope: Section 5, p.20: the paper says it validated the approach on the one complex MCL1-19G.
bensberg-transfer-learning-training-setu: Sections 2.4/2.5 and 3.2: fixed weight fraction, first layer and standardization not varied, CoRe state reloaded, 300 steps on all energies; all stated.
bensberg-mlp-architecture-ensemble: Section 3.2, p.11: ensemble of 10, c=2, eeACSF input, 90/10 split per member; stated.
bensberg-energy-difference-definition: Section 4.1, p.13: the two stated differences (def2-TZVP vs def2-SVP, and two DLPNO-CCSD(T0) cores) are the paper's own account of what is compared.
bensberg-training-set-size: Section 4.2, p.14: 8417 and 5285 conformers, 44 QM atoms; stated.
bensberg-protonation-error-cancellation-: Section 4.4, p.18: the paper itself states the ligand protonation state is unclear and the agreement may have benefited from error cancellation.
bensberg-future-active-learning: Section 5, p.21: the paper states active learning is future work to lower the computational cost of its own approach, which is a stated cost limit. Borderline: it is a plan more than a limit.
bensberg-derivatives-unavailable: Section 5, p.21 and Section 4.3, p.16: the paper states analytic derivatives are unavailable, and forces are not available in its own QM/QM/MM implementation.
bentellis-hardware-selection: Section II, p.2: the paper states the two processors were chosen for availability and that the newest IBM processor was not used because of queue times.
bentellis-scope-h2-no-scaling: Introduction and Section II: the paper states it studies H2 only and does not analyze hardware scaling (repeated in Section IV).
bentellis-aqt-marmot-spec: Section II.A: 40Ca+ ions, up to 16 qubits, all-to-all, basis gates [rx, rz, rxx] in Qiskit; stated as the study's setup.
bentellis-ibmq-manila-setup: Section II.B: all runs on ibmq manila (Falcon r.11L), minimal time between runs, average T1 169 us and T2 76 us; stated.
bentellis-ansatz-rycnot: Section III.B: the paper states it used RYCNOT (four RY, circular CNOT layer) and gives its reason (UCCSD depth, 92 for ibmq manila).
bentellis-hamiltonian-setup: Section III.C and Fig. 6: 4-qubit H2 Hamiltonian, STO-3g, 0.735 Angstrom, E_FCI = -1.136189454088 Ha.
bentellis-hamiltonian-prefactors: Appendix B: the eight coefficients are listed and the Hamiltonian is stated to come from Qiskit's PySCF extension.
bentellis-experimental-settings: Section IV: the settings list (RY-CNOT, NFT, Qiskit, 200 shots, no mitigation, 15 iterations) is stated for all runs.
bentellis-no-native-error-mitigation-aqt: Section IV: the paper states AQT hardware does not natively support error mitigation, so aqt marmot results are unmitigated.
bentellis-not-a-hardware-recommendation: Section VI (end): the paper states the results cannot be used as a hardware recommendation because they depend on processor, calibration, algorithm and optimizer.
bentellis-no-generalization: Section V, Conclusion: the paper states its results apply only to these two processor types and this algorithm, and cannot directly be generalized.
coherent-control-error-definition: Section I, Eq. (1): the paper defines the coherent control error.
noise-assumptions-minimal: Section II: the paper states it assumes only ||eps||_inf <= bound, not equal errors or a small bound.
generality-of-results: Introduction: the paper states the conditions its results cover (independent noise, arbitrary unitaries, no assumption on the nature of the noise).
theorem-II-1-fidelity-from-lipschitz: Theorem II.1, Section II: stated with its conditions (L a Lipschitz bound, ||eps||_inf <= bound, any initial state) and proved in the following lines.
theorem-II-2-norm-lipschitz-bound: Theorem II.2, Section II: stated for any eps, eps' and initial state; proved in Appendix A.
proof-technique-theorem-II-2: Appendix A: the proof bounds dU_i/d eps_i by ||H_i||, then uses the triangle inequality, unitarity and submultiplicativity inductively, as the value says.
single-z-rotation-sensitivity: Section II, Eq. (19): follows directly from the proved Theorem II.2 for U = Rz(theta); the value speaks of the bound's sensitivity, which is exact algebra.
theorem-II-3-odd-case-not-proved: Appendix D, first line: the paper states it proves only (23a) and that (23b) follows by trivial modifications.
pairwise-future-work: Section II.C, end: the paper states it mainly uses the norm-based bounds and leaves the analogous conclusions for pair-wise bounds to future research.
global-phase-dependence-of-bounds: Section II.B, Eqs. (20)-(22): independence of the noisy circuit from the offset is shown by Eq. (21); the dependence of ||H|| on the offset is immediate; Theorem II.2 is stated to hold for any shifted H_i, so the tightest bound is the minimizing offset.
tightness-no-multi-gate-exact: Appendix C: the paper states that for N>1 an explicit expression for the exact worst-case fidelity is more involved, so the bound is only a lower bound.
diamond-distance-from-lipschitz: Section III, Eq. (28): the chain of inequalities that gives the diamond-distance bound (with a sqrt(d) factor the value omits) is shown in the text.
scalability-proposition-B1: Appendix B, Proposition B.1: stated with its condition (gate acts on a subset of qubits) and proved in the next lines.
qft-gate-sets-and-simulation-setup: Section V: five gate sets, BQSKit at maximum level, noise uniform in [-0.05, 0.05], Haar-random initial states, 40,000 runs; all stated.
qft-bound-conservative: Section V: the paper states its own worst-case fidelity bound is conservative and negative for four of five circuits.
qft-no-general-gate-set-claim: Section V: the paper states it does not claim gate set E is generally preferable and that a better circuit on set D may exist.
hardware-setup-ibm-nairobi: Section VI and Appendix F: 16 noise levels, 80 samples, Rz errors only, single-qubit tomography, 153,600,000 circuits in total.
vqa-lipschitz-bound-parametrized: Section VI, Eq. (32): a direct application of the proved Theorem II.2 to theta_i H_i; the value is limited to the bound.
vqa-regression-experiment-setup: Section VI: single qubit, sine regression, 20 points, five lambda values, eight models per lambda, 50 ADAM iterations, noise bound 0.05 on Ry and Rz.
berberich-2024-conclusion-future-work: Section VII: the paper names these as next steps, which it states as not yet done.
bound-not-tight: Section II.B: the paper states the bound (17) is in general not tight because gate coupling is ignored.
model-class-trainable-encoding: Section II, Eqs. (2)-(4): the paper defines the model class it studies.
lipschitz-bound-eq5-independent-of-theta: Section II, Eq. (5): proved in Appendix A.2 (Jacobian bound, then composition with the measurement map); independence from theta_j is visible in the formula.
worst-case-robustness-from-lipschitz: Section III, Eq. (7): follows directly from the definition of a Lipschitz bound (Eq. 1); the value is limited to the worst-case guarantee.
regularized-training-objective: Section III, Eq. (9): the paper defines its regularized training problem.
circle-experiment-setup: Section III and Appendix C: domain, radius 2/pi, labels, SU(2) gates, 3 qubits, nearest-neighbour CNOTs, 3 layers, Z x Z x Z; all stated.
generalization-tradeoff-expressivity: Section IV: the paper states the caveat that a too small Lipschitz bound can make the generalization bound meaningless.
direct-lambda-effect-open: Section IV: the paper states the direct effect of lambda on generalization is not yet studied and is expected to be nontrivial.
numerics-setup-optimizer: Appendix C.1: PennyLane, noiseless lightning.qubit, ADAM with rate 0.1, 200 epochs, 12 models per lambda, minimal cost kept; all stated.
scope-illustration-only: Section VI: the paper states the numerics are for illustration and the theory covers all models of form (4).
future-work-nonlinear-encodings: Section VI: the paper states it considers only affine encodings and names nonlinear encodings as future work; it also says the principles are transferable to kernel and linear models.
norm-choice-future: Section III: the paper states it uses 2-norms and that other norms are a future direction.
observable-not-optimized: Section III: the paper states it does not optimize over M, so the regularization does not involve M.
hardware-vs-data-robustness: Section I: the paper states that data-perturbation robustness is its subject and is independent of hardware-error robustness.
fixed-encoding-lipschitz-not-tunable: Section V: follows from Eq. (5), proved in Appendix A.2; for model (14) the w_j are fixed a priori, so the bound is fixed. The statement is limited to the Lipschitz bound.
lipschitz-bound-trainable-encoding: Eq. (5), proved in Appendix A.2, depends on ||w_j|| ||H_j||; with Eq. (7) this gives the robustness guarantee. 'Crucial impact' is the authors' emphasis on that bound.
pennylane-backprop-simulator-drawbacks: Section on backpropagation: the paper states the drawbacks of its own backprop path on simulators (memory scaling, no hardware support).
pennylane-shift-extensions-not-implement: Section on derivatives: the paper states these extensions are not currently implemented. The text layer splices footnote 8 (non- at the foot of the page) into this line, so the non-equidistant reading is right.
pennylane-derivatives-are-estimates: Footnote 7: the paper states what it means by derivatives (estimates, approximate even with exact expectations).
pennylane-finite-difference-noise-tradeo: Section on numerical derivatives: the paper states the tradeoff in the choice of the difference on noisy hardware; the black-box property is part of the method's description.
pennylane-sampling-not-differentiable: Section on measurement returns: the paper states returning samples is not differentiable.

theory_low.lipschitz-example-comparison: The Lipschitz bounds (3 pi/8 against 5 pi/8) follow from Theorem II.2, but 'explains why the first is more robust' is the authors' interpretation: a smaller worst-case bound does not by itself prove greater actual robustness. The support is a measured result.
theory_low.pairwise-theorem-II-3: The value overstates. Appendix D proves only the even case (23a). The odd case (23b) is asserted to follow with trivial modifications and is not proved in the paper.
theory_low.pairwise-fidelity-bound-even-n: The value bundles an interpretation. Eq. (24) combines Theorem II.3 (even case, proved) with Theorem II.1, but 'this shows the coupling influences robustness' is the authors' reading of a bound. A worst-case bound that depends on coupling does not show the actual robustness depends on it.
theory_low.pairwise-vs-sum-strictness: The inequality itself is shown, but 'strict in almost all cases' is an informal argument (strict when a,b>0 and when the top eigenvectors are linearly independent) with no proof of 'almost all'. An informal bound argument is not a proved result.
theory_low.tightness-single-gate: Appendix C says 'it is not hard to show' that the worst-case fidelity equals |cos(||H|| eps)| for N=1 and ||H|| eps <= pi/2. No proof is given. The Taylor-approximation remark follows from that unproved claim.
theory_low.tightness-bound-18-vs-C2: The comparison uses (C2), which rests on the unproved (C1), and replaces sin(x) by x for small noise. It is an approximate small-noise argument. The paper says thus proven, but the step is not rigorous.
theory_low.fidelity-bounds-hamiltonian-norms: The Abstract and Conclusion say the resilience is 'mainly influenced' by the Hamiltonian norms. What is proved is Theorem II.2, a worst-case bound that depends on the norms. The paper itself says the bound is not tight and that gate coupling also matters (Theorem II.3). 'Mainly influenced' is the authors' interpretation of a bound. Set LOW at the team lead's decision, 2026-10-31 (Sprint 14 Manual Validation Q1 option 1).
theory_low.theorem-iv1-informal: This is the informal version. It drops the conditions (loss Lipschitz, compact Z, probability 1 - delta) and leaves C1 and C2 unspecified. The proved statement is Theorem B.1.
theory_low.theorem-b1-statement: cross-group consistency, Rule A (coordinator, 2026-10-30): Theorem B.1, App. B, pp.8-9: proved by combining the Lipschitz bound (5) with Lemma B.1, and Lemma B.1 rests on Theorems 1 and 6 of Xu and Mannor [7], cited and not proved here.
theory_low.lemma-b1-statement: cross-group consistency, Rule A (coordinator, 2026-10-30): Lemma B.1, App. B, p.8: after the Lipschitz step (B6), the proof uses '[7, Theorem 6]' to obtain (K, epsilon)-robustness and '[7, Theorem 1]' for the probability bound. Both are theorems of Xu and Mannor [7], cited and not proved in this paper; the bound rests on them.
theory_low.generalization-bound-converges: cross-group consistency, Rule A (coordinator, 2026-10-30): App. B, Eqs. (B8)-(B9), p.9: the convergence uses the covering-number bound '[61, Lemma 6.27]', cited, inserted into Theorem B.1, which itself rests on Theorems 1 and 6 of Xu and Mannor [7], cited.
theory_low.fixed-encoding-reg-phi-no-effect: Part of the value is proved (regularizing phi leaves the bound (5) unchanged). 'Therefore cannot be used to improve robustness' is the authors' inference from a bound. An upper bound that does not change does not prove the true robustness does not change.
theory_low.generalization-bound-involves-encoding: Theorem IV.1, Sec. IV, p.4, proved as Theorem B.1, App. B, pp.8-9: the bound containing the sum of ||w_j|| ||H_j|| is obtained from Lemma B.1, whose probability bound is '[7, Theorem 6]' and '[7, Theorem 1]' of Xu and Mannor, cited and not proved here. Set LOW at the team lead's decision, 2026-10-31 (Sprint 14 Manual Validation Q1 option 1).
